title: HTTP — every way a request can go wrong, told apart
description: Drives the debug client through each outcome it distinguishes, against a real simulator on 127.0.0.1:18080: a route edited to 503 answers as an HTTP error with its status; a route edited to a status the server refuses stops being served while the simulator stays up, so the client meets a 404; a URL that is not absolute is refused before anything is sent; a port nothing listens on fails with no status; a simulator switched off fails the same way; and switching it back on brings the next request through with no action on the client. Real clock — a stepped host does not move its virtual clock while a request is open, so every latency would read zero, and the refused requests end on the client's real-time bounds either way. Every value a drive changes is read with a wait on a value only that drive can produce, so no step reads a verdict left over from the one before, or a sibling property not yet published. The two summaries publish at most every 30 seconds, so a wait on one of their counts allows 45: the interval, the tick that assigns it, and margin.

judge.text: An HTTP error and a failure read differently in the Status pill: the first means the server was reached and answered outside 2xx, the second that no answer arrived at all.
A timeout is deliberately not driven: the simulator answers every request it accepts, so nothing on this bench holds a request open. The unit tests drive it on a virtual clock.
